p01-ruler-title.name: p01-ruler-title
p01-ruler-title.text: The standard deviation is a ruler: $z$ tells how many rulers a value is from the mean

p01-ruler-ctx.name: p01-ruler-ctx
p01-ruler-ctx.text: 5 measurements 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. First find the mean and the ruler length, then measure each value with the ruler.

p01-ruler-defn.name: p01-ruler-defn
p01-ruler-defn.text: $\bar x=\frac{1}{N}\sum x_i$　　$\sigma=\sqrt{\frac{1}{N-1}\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2}$　　$z_i=\frac{x_i-\bar x}{\sigma}$ (how many standard deviations value $i$ is from the mean)

p01-ruler-tk.name: p01-ruler-tk
p01-ruler-tk.text: 20 is 20 below the mean: $\frac{20-40}{15.811}=-1.265$, i.e. 1.265 rulers to the left of the mean

p02-pull-title.name: p02-pull-title
p02-pull-title.text: One bad point pulls both the mean and the "ruler" off

p02-pull-ctx.name: p02-pull-ctx
p02-pull-ctx.text: 9 normal values 10, 11, 12, then one spike 101 mixed in. Squaring magnifies large deviations: $2^2=4$, $100^2=10000$.

p02-pull-defn.name: p02-pull-defn
p02-pull-defn.text: Mean $\bar x=\frac{\sum x_i}{N}$　　Sample variance $s^2=\frac{SS}{N-1}$, $SS=\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2$　　$\sigma=\sqrt{s^2}$

p02-pull-t10b.name: p02-pull-t10b
p02-pull-t10b.text: $\bar x=\frac{98+101}{10}=19.9$: no data point is near here

p03-mask-title.name: p03-mask-title
p03-mask-title.text: The $3\sigma$ rule lets 101 pass: it stretches the ruler and hides inside it

p03-mask-ctx.name: p03-mask-ctx
p03-mask-ctx.text: Rule: suspect if $|z|>3$ (about 99% within $3\sigma$ if normal). Same 101, three rulers: with 101 mean 19.9, $\sigma=$28.51; normal 9: 10.89, 0.78 (page 2).

p03-mask-zr.name: p03-mask-zr
p03-mask-zr.text: Suspicious　$|z|>3$ (the chart goes up to $z=6$, longer bars are truncated)

p03-mask-mad.name: p03-mask-mad
p03-mask-mad.text: MAD = the median of the absolute deviations of the values from the median: $|x-11|$ sorted gives 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 90, with median $=1$; the median $=11$ (the 5th and 6th sorted values are both 11)

p04-keep-title.name: p04-keep-title
p04-keep-title.text: After catching it, delete or keep? First ask where it came from

p04-keep-ctx.name: p04-keep-ctx
p04-keep-ctx.text: Different sources, different treatment; when keeping long-tailed data, switch to a cost in which "large errors do not explode".

p04-keep-q.name: p04-keep-q
p04-keep-q.text: Where did this outlier come from?

p04-keep-lt.name: p04-keep-lt
p04-keep-lt.text:
A real long tail
(a few high-income households)
⇒ keep, use the Huber cost

p04-keep-hdef.name: p04-keep-hdef
p04-keep-hdef.text: Squared cost $\frac{1}{2}e^2$　　Huber ($\delta=1$, beyond error 1 it goes straight): $\frac{1}{2}e^2$ ($|e|\leq 1$), $|e|-\frac{1}{2}$ ($|e|>1$)

p04-keep-tbt.name: p04-keep-tbt
p04-keep-tbt.text: Long tail: fewer and fewer to the right, but real

p05-units-title.name: p05-units-title
p05-units-title.text: With different units, the "nearest person" changes

p05-units-ctx.name: p05-units-ctx
p05-units-ctx.text: 5 users and the query person "Q". In the left chart both axes use the same ruler (1 currency unit = 1 year = 1 unit); in the right chart both axes are in units of $\sigma$.

p05-units-defn.name: p05-units-defn
p05-units-defn.text: Euclidean distance $d=\sqrt{(\Delta x_1)^2+(\Delta x_2)^2}$; $z$ distance: first turn each feature into $z=\frac{x-\bar x}{\sigma}$, then compute $d$

p05-units-lt.name: p05-units-lt
p05-units-lt.text: Raw units: horizontal = annual income, vertical = age (same ruler)

p05-units-rt.name: p05-units-rt
p05-units-rt.text: After z-score: horizontal = income z, vertical = age z

p06-three-title.name: p06-three-title
p06-three-title.text: Three normalizations: the same 5 values land on different rulers

p06-three-ctx.name: p06-three-ctx
p06-three-ctx.text: First three rows are aligned: the same $x$ has the same position in raw, $z$ and min-max; softmax is not aligned, both ends squeezed to the middle.

p06-three-labs.name: p06-three-labs
p06-three-labs.text:
softmax scaling ($r$ sets the width of the linear part, here 1; the formula is the sigmoid): $y=\frac{x-40}{15.811}$, $\frac{1}{1+e^{-y}}$
Example: $y=-1.265$ → $0.220$

p06-three-jz.name: p06-three-jz
p06-three-jz.text: z: no fixed bounds; one extreme value can still pull $\bar x,\sigma$ off

p06-three-jm.name: p06-three-jm
p06-three-jm.text: min-max: with 101 included, 12 becomes $\frac{12-10}{101-10}=0.022$ and the rest are squeezed into a lump

p06-three-js.name: p06-three-js
p06-three-js.text: softmax: both ends are squeezed into $(0,1)$, good for long tails; this row is not aligned with the first three

p07-leak-title.name: p07-leak-title
p07-leak-title.text: Parameters may only come from the training set: otherwise the shift of the test set is erased

p07-leak-ctx.name: p07-leak-ctx
p07-leak-ctx.text: Training set 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 ($\bar x=40$, $\sigma=15.811$); test set 70, 80, 90, a whole batch that is too high.

p07-leak-lb.name: p07-leak-lb
p07-leak-lb.text: Wrong: use the test set's own $\bar x=\frac{70+80+90}{3}=80$, $\sigma=\sqrt{\frac{(-10)^2+0+10^2}{2}}=10$

p07-leak-fw.name: p07-leak-fw
p07-leak-fw.text: $\frac{70-80}{10}=-1$, $\frac{80-80}{10}=0$, $\frac{90-80}{10}=1$: all fall inside the training range, the shift disappears

p08-miss-title.name: p08-miss-title
p08-miss-title.text: Data is missing: three approaches, where is it filled?

p08-miss-ctx.name: p08-miss-ctx
p08-miss-ctx.text: Cholesterol (mg/dL) of 10 patients: 8 have values, 2 are missing. Blue dots = values actually measured (equal values stacked upward).

p08-miss-l1.name: p08-miss-l1
p08-miss-l1.text: ① Delete: throw away the 2 missing rows entirely, leaving $N=8$

p08-miss-l2.name: p08-miss-l2
p08-miss-l2.text: ② Mean imputation: fill both with $\bar x=\frac{180+190+200+210+220+180+200+220}{8}=200$ (180+190+200+210+220+180+200+220 = the sum of the 8 values; red squares stacked on the mean)

p08-miss-l3.name: p08-miss-l3
p08-miss-l3.text: ③ Multiple imputation: draw 2 values from $N(200,\,16.04^2)$, 3 sets (teaching setup, seed 0); $16.04=\sqrt{\frac{1800}{7}}$ is the sample standard deviation of the 8 values; the sets show how imputation uncertainty changes the result (pages 9–10)

p09-shrink-title.name: p09-shrink-title
p09-shrink-title.text: Mean imputation: the mean does not change, but the variance is lowered by 22.2%

p09-shrink-ctx.name: p09-shrink-ctx
p09-shrink-ctx.text: $s^2=\frac{SS}{N-1}$. The two imputed 200s are $0$ from the mean, so $SS$ stays but $N$ grows. Each of the three bar groups is scaled on its own.

p09-shrink-jud.name: p09-shrink-jud
p09-shrink-jud.text: Sum of squares unchanged, denominator larger ⇒ variance falls by $1-\frac{200.00}{257.14}=22.2\%$

p10-mi-title.name: p10-mi-title
p10-mi-title.text: Multiple imputation: count "the imputed values are guesses" in the standard error

p10-mi-ctx.name: p10-mi-ctx
p10-mi-ctx.text: Standard error of the mean $SE=\sqrt{s^2/N}$. Rubin's combination: $T=\bar U+(1+\frac{1}{m})B$, $SE=\sqrt T$.

p10-mi-defn.name: p10-mi-defn
p10-mi-defn.text: $\bar U$ = the average of $\frac{s^2}{N}$ of each completed data set (within); $B$ = the variation among the set means (between, reflecting the uncertainty of imputation)

p10-mi-refl.name: p10-mi-refl
p10-mi-refl.text: $SE=5.67$ with observed values only (reference line). The aim of MI is to be more honest than mean imputation (4.65 > 4.47); it need not return to 5.67; the sampling of $m=3$ sets also fluctuates

p10-mi-ub.name: p10-mi-ub
p10-mi-ub.text: The three sets of imputed values on page 8, each combined with the 8 observed to make 10 values, give means 199.99, 201.20, 199.72 → $B=0.616$; the $s^2/N$ of each set is 20.095, 21.045, 21.185 → $\bar U=20.775$

p11-pipe-title.name: p11-pipe-title
p11-pipe-title.text: Order: outliers → missing values → normalization; parameters are learned from the training set only

p11-pipe-ctx.name: p11-pipe-ctx
p11-pipe-ctx.text: The top row is the processing flow of the training set and the bottom row is the test set: it applies the same parameters learned in the top row.

p11-pipe-bk0.name: p11-pipe-bk0
p11-pipe-bk0.text:
1 Outliers
Check the source first, then decide

p11-pipe-bk1.name: p11-pipe-bk1
p11-pipe-bk1.text:
2 Missing values
Fill with the training $\bar x=200$

p11-pipe-rs1.name: p11-pipe-rs1
p11-pipe-rs1.text: Imputation should use a clean mean

p11-pipe-rs2.name: p11-pipe-rs2
p11-pipe-rs2.text: $\bar x,\sigma$ must be computed on the completed data

p11-pipe-tk1.name: p11-pipe-tk1
p11-pipe-tk1.text:
2 Missing values
Apply the training parameters

p11-pipe-pm.name: p11-pipe-pm
p11-pipe-pm.text: Dashed line = parameters learned on the training set passed to the test set; the test set does not relearn

p12-code-title.name: p12-code-title
p12-code-title.text: scikit-learn: chain the three steps into one pipeline

p12-code-ctx.name: p12-code-ctx
p12-code-ctx.text: The training data is the 8 cholesterol values of page 8 plus 2 missing ones. The output of the actually run program is in the comments.

p12-code-code.name: p12-code-code
p12-code-code.text:
```
# X_train: the 10 values of page 8 (2 of them NaN); X_test: [[NaN], [240]]
pipe = make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy='mean'),
                     StandardScaler())
pipe.fit(X_train)            # learn parameters from the training set only
pipe.transform(X_test)       # apply the same parameters to the test set
# imputation mean 200.0; standard deviation 13.416 (divides by N)
# test values [NaN, 240] → [0.0, 2.981]
```

p12-code-nt.name: p12-code-nt
p12-code-nt.text:
Test value 240: $\frac{240-200}{13.416}=2.981$; NaN is first imputed as 200, then $\frac{200-200}{13.416}=0$
Hand-computed $\sigma$ divides by $N-1$: the completed 10 values give $\sqrt{\frac{1800}{9}}=14.142$; the tool divides by $N$: $\sqrt{\frac{1800}{10}}=13.416$ (different convention, not an error)
Outliers (step 1) are not in this pipeline and must be handled first by yourself

p13-practice1-title.name: p13-practice1-title
p13-practice1-title.text: Exercise 1: the sensor has an extra 116

p13-practice1-ctx.name: p13-practice1-ctx
p13-practice1-ctx.text: A sensor collects $\{20,21,22,21,116\}$. Think first, then press Next for feedback.

p13-practice1-q1.name: p13-practice1-q1
p13-practice1-q1.text: Question 1: what is the mean including 116? What is the mean after removing 116?

p13-practice1-q2.name: p13-practice1-q2
p13-practice1-q2.text: Question 2: compute the $z$ of 116 from the mean and $\sigma$ including it ($\sigma$ divides by $N-1$); does the $3\sigma$ rule catch it? Then remove 116 and re-measure with the other 4 values.

p14-practice2-title.name: p14-practice2-title
p14-practice2-title.text: Exercise 2: transform new values with the training parameters

p14-practice2-ctx.name: p14-practice2-ctx
p14-practice2-ctx.text: Think first, then press Next for feedback.

p14-practice2-q1.name: p14-practice2-q1
p14-practice2-q1.text: Question 3: the training set has $\bar x=100$, $\sigma=20$. What are the $z$ of $x=140$ and $x=70$?

p14-practice2-q2.name: p14-practice2-q2
p14-practice2-q2.text: Question 4: training min 20, max 60. What are the min-max values of test values 70 and 10? Do they fall in $[0,1]$?

p15-practice3-title.name: p15-practice3-title
p15-practice3-title.text: Exercise 3: what is the variance after filling in the mean?

p15-practice3-ctx.name: p15-practice3-ctx
p15-practice3-ctx.text: 5 patients, the 5th is missing; the other 4 values are 10, 12, 14, 16. Think first, then press Next for feedback.

p15-practice3-q.name: p15-practice3-q
p15-practice3-q.text: Question 5: fill the 5th with the mean of the 4. What is the variance $s^2=\frac{SS}{N-1}$ after filling? By what % is it smaller than the $s^2$ with only 4?

p15-practice3-a1.name: p15-practice3-a1
p15-practice3-a1.text:
Filled in $\bar x=\frac{10+12+14+16}{4}=13$
$SS=(-3)^2+(-1)^2+1^2+3^2=20$ (the imputed 13 has deviation 0)

p16-summary-title.name: p16-summary-title
p16-summary-title.text: The whole KP02: clean the data first, so the later statistics can be trusted

p16-summary-ctx.name: p16-summary-ctx
p16-summary-ctx.text: Every cell is the conclusion of an earlier page; below is the next question it must answer.

p16-summary-ch1.name: p16-summary-ch1
p16-summary-ch1.text:
Outliers (pages 2–4)
Pull $\bar x$ off,
stretch $\sigma$
ask the source first

p16-summary-ch2.name: p16-summary-ch2
p16-summary-ch2.text:
Units (pages 5–6)
Large units dominate distance
use $z$ for the same scale

p16-summary-ch3.name: p16-summary-ch3
p16-summary-ch3.text:
Leakage (page 7)
Parameters learned from
the training set only

p16-summary-next.name: p16-summary-next
p16-summary-next.text:
The next KP asks: the data is clean, does a single feature really discriminate?
Is the mean difference of two classes real or luck? ⇒ examine features one by one with hypothesis tests
